 Hearst Television’s Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early and mail-in ballots.
 Advertisement Updated: 8:34 PM PDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Daniel Macht Digital Media Manager Track early voting in California for the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
 Hearst Television’s Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early and mail-in ballots.
 Updated: 8:34 PM PDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Daniel Macht Digital Media Manager Early voting is underway in California and many other states for the Nov. 3 midterm election.
 The election will decide the balance of power in Congress. In California, voters will also select the next governor and other statewide officeholders. State propositions and local measures are also in play. 
 Advertisement California voter guide 2026: What to know about the propositions and races on the November ballot Hearst Television’s Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early and mail-in ballots, with data that comes from the University of Florida Election Lab.
 The election lab has tracked early voting data since 2008 and also aggregates turnout and results data. Early voting counts are compiled directly from state and regional sources. 
 See the graphic below for more information on the early vote in California and across the nation. The graphic also shows the early vote as a share of the 2022 turnout. 
 In California, Political Data Inc. also tracks the early vote. 
 You can see the data firm’s latest updates here . 
 As of Sunday, Oct. 23, the overall turnout rate in California was 12%. 
 Here are other early voting trends: 
 By party: 
 Democrats have returned 1,417,109 ballots for a turnout rate of 14%
 Republicans have returned 826,230 ballots for a turnout rate of 14%
 Other groups of voters have returned 591,156 ballots for a turnout rate of 8%
 For age groups:
 Voters ages 65 or older had the highest turnout so far at 26%
 Voters ages 50-64 had a turnout rate of 13%
 Voters ages 35-39 had a turnout rate of 7%
 The turnout rate for those 18-34 was lowest at 4%
 By ethnicity: 
 White voters had the highest turnout rate so far at 15%
 Asian voters had a turnout rate of 12% 
 Black voters had a turnout rate of 10% 
 Latino voters had the lowest turnout rate at 8%
